To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the adenovirus 9ORF protein binds the PDZ domain of the DLG protein, and this interaction is conserved in other human virus oncoprotein-DLG interactions.
the human virus oncoprotein 9ORF-1 interacts with DLG and that the human viruses human T cell leukemia type 1 virus and human papilloma virus type 18 E6 oncoprotein interact with DLG.
the human adenovirus 9ORF 1 protein and several different human viral oncoproteins interact with the PDZ-domain-containing protein DLG.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the discovery and characterization of cellular proteins that associate with human virus oncoprotein C termini and the identification of viral C-terminal regions required for these interactions.
the identification of cellular targets for viral oncoproteins and with understanding how these interactions contribute to the transforming activities of these proteins.
the identification of novel cellular proteins that interact with viral proteins and the characterization of their roles in the viral life cycle.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the 9BP- 1 protein is a novel PDZ domain-containing cellular protein that binds to the 9ORFI oncoprotein and that the 9orf1 protein binds to the hDlg/SAP 97 protein, and that both the 9BP1 and hDlg/SAP-97 proteins are cellular proteins.

the 9BP- 1 protein binds to a 9ORFI C-terminal region that contains a consensus PDZ domain-binding motif, that 9ORFI and other viral oncoproteins bind to DLG, and that the 9 ORFI and other viral proteins bind to PDZ domains of DLG.
9ORF binds to hDlg/Sap97, and that the interaction is mediated through the PDZ domain of hDlg/Sap-97.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
9ORF 1, Tax, and HPV 18 E6 are able to bind to hDlg/Sap97, a mammalain homolog of the discs large tumor suppressors protein, through a conserved C-terminal PDZ domain binding motif.
the adenoviral oncoprotein 9ORF 1 binds to hDlg/Sap 97 and that the binding is mediated through the PDZ domain.

the 9BP- 1 and DLG genes encode cellular proteins which bind the 9ORFI and E4-9ORF1 proteins, respectively, and that the 9 ORF1 protein, which is expressed from an adenovirus type 9 early region gene, binds the cellular protein DLG.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the C terminus of the human virus oncoprotein 9ORF-1 is required for transformation and that the C termini of several different human oncoproteins contain consensus PDZ domain-binding sequences.
the PDZ domains of DLG are important in mediating the transformation activities of adenovirus E1A, E4 9ORF-1, human T cell lymphotropic virus type I Tax, and human papilloma virus E6 oncoprotein.
the C-terminal PDZ-binding motif is not only conserved among the human virus oncoprotein family, but is also a common theme among cellular oncoproteins.
